marker.step_source:
import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

output.meta_commit_message: feat(triage): keep one task-triage notification row per bead across re-presentations

marker.step_source:
head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

**Measurements (read-only, last 30 days):**
- athena: 1,118 triage notification rows, about 36 a day, averaging 2.35 rows per bead and gate kind (worst case 27). apollo looks the same: 978 rows, 2.42 per bead and kind, worst 27.
- New +1 evidence caused 72% of the 2,142 cancel-and-recreate cycles. The rest were notes, description, refs and typed-field edits.
- 112 recreations changed nothing visible. All of them fell in four one-hour bursts, which points to code or version bumps rather than bead edits.
- So almost all churn comes from changes the gate really shows. Hashing fewer fields alone would not have helped; one row per bead was the actual fix.

**What changed:**
- **One row per bead:** when a pending gate's content changes, the replacement gate takes over the old notification row instead of adding a new one. The row keeps its read, dismissed and snoozed state, and there is no new toast or sound. The old gate is then cancelled without dismissing the shared row.
- **When a new row still appears:** a new unread row is created only when the gate kind changes (snooze or wake) or the bead becomes ready again.
- **Failure handling:** if creating the replacement fails, the old gate stays tracked and the next pass retries. The existing recovery for request-id conflicts still works.
- **Fingerprint:** the change hash now covers only what each gate kind displays. In practice that only drops +1 evidence and close history from flag-removal gates. Every existing task-triage and snooze fingerprint is byte-identical to before (I checked against the old code), so installing won't recreate all ~430 pending gates at once.

- I did not rerun the full 47-minute check after the last small edit to `service_creation.py`.

**Things to know:**
